title: Molecular Characterization of Lineage-IV Peste Des Petits Ruminants Virus and Development of IELISA
author: Kamal, Khan, et al.
materials: All swabs and tissue samples were subjected to RNA extraction according to the manufacturer’s instructions using a commercial RNA extraction (Ambien Pure Link RNA) Mini Kit. Reagent contamination was detected using a negative control. Extracted RNA was eluted in 50 µL nuclease-free water, which was then stored at -70 °C until used., A NanoDrop(Thermo Scientific, Wilmington, DE, USA) measured the eluted RNA concentration and a conc. of ~ 2.0 or (100ng/ul)viral RNA was used for RT-PCR. A swab was obtained from clinically healthy sheep negative for cELISA and was considered a negative control. The synthesis of the cDNA of PPRV was performed according to the manufacturer’s instructions of Revert Ad First Strand cDNA(Thermo-Scientific) [20].

The swabs and tissue samples were processed following the standard procedures [26] and inoculum was prepared for PPR virus recovery. Briefly, sub-cultures were performed using pre-cultured Vero cells (ATCC-USA). Before inoculating the Vero cell line, the medium was decanted and inoculum was dispensed (1 ml) after filtering through 0.2 μm syringe filters (Millipore). Vero cells (ATCC, USA) were grown in Dulbecco Minimum Essential Medium (100 ml of DMEM) containing10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) and 2% of pen-strep antibiotics (Corning, USA) [26]. Confluent monolayers of Vero cells were infected with previously processed and filtered tissue and swab samples. These were then incubated at 37 °C for two hours before being washed with PBS and supplemented with DMEM (maintenance media). The infected Vero cells were maintained at 37 °C for seven days and evaluated daily for any cytopathic effects (CPE). The specimen was regarded as negative when the CPE was not observed after consecutive three blind passages. The PPRV isolates were confirmed based on specific CPE and by using ‘N’ gene-based RT-PCR. The CPE, induced by Morbillivirus, triggered cell rounding and syncytia formation. The cells undergo three cycles of freezing and thawing, followed by centrifugation. The resultant supernatants were used for RNA extraction.

Sequencing was conducted and sequence data analysis was conducted following standard procedures [22, 26]. Sequence alignment was carried out using CLUSTALX software. In addition, sequenced data of Pakistani isolates were compared with other related sequences retrieved from the Gene Bank. The variations among N-gene sequences and the phylogenetic tree (analysis) of PPRV isolates used in the current study were constructed using the neighbour-joining technique in Mega-X (10.2.2). Bootstrap verification of the resulting phylogenetic tree was performed by analysis of 100 bootstraps. Given the expected similar genetic patterns, only three representative samples were randomly selected for sequencing (one from each sample collection area). Furthermore, the PCR amplicons were purified using the QIAEXII PCR purification kit (Qiagen, Venlo, Netherlands) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Purified PCR products were sent for sequencing by Macrogen (Korea). Genius software was used to submit the sequencing to NCBI to obtain new accession numbers for our isolates from the current study.

The highest dilution of positive serum produced the highest optical density (OD), making it the best concentration for our research. Figure 7 shows that the same dilution produced the best antigen and antibody working solutions for the ELISA experiment in negative serum. Furthermore, duplicate serum samples (including positive and negative standards) were simultaneously added to three plates. No significant variation was observed in these plates. To assess the diagnostic efficacy of the IELISA assay, 325 serum samples were tested in parallel with the commercially available kit. The efficacy of IELISA was compared with a commercial kit employing all 325 serum samples.

steps.title: Extract RNA from samples
steps.instruction: Use the Ambien PureLink RNA Mini Kit (manufacturer’s protocol) to extract RNA from all swabs and tissue samples, include a negative control to monitor reagent contamination, elute RNA in 50 µL nuclease‑free water and store at –70 °C.

substeps.instruction: Prepare samples and reagents according to kit instructions.
Process a negative control alongside the specimens.
Elute the purified RNA in exactly 50 µL nuclease‑free water.
Aliquot and freeze the eluate at –70 °C until further use.

steps.title: Quantify and select RNA for RT‑PCR
steps.instruction: Measure RNA concentration with a NanoDrop spectrophotometer (Thermo Scientific); use approximately 2.0 µg/µL (≈100 ng/µL) viral RNA for downstream RT‑PCR, and keep a swab from a clinically healthy, cELISA‑negative sheep as a negative control.

steps.title: Synthesize cDNA
steps.instruction: Perform first‑strand cDNA synthesis using the RevertAid First Strand cDNA Synthesis Kit (Thermo‑Scientific) following the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Validate cDNA by RT‑PCR
steps.instruction: Run the RT‑PCR protocol described in the Materials and Methods section on the synthesized cDNA to confirm its quality and quantity before proceeding with further experiments.

steps.title: Isolate and propagate PPRV in Vero cells
steps.instruction: Process swabs/tissues per standard procedures, filter inoculum through a 0.2 µm Millipore syringe filter, dispense 1 mL onto confluent Vero cell monolayers (ATCC‑USA) grown in 100 mL DMEM with 10 % FBS and 2 % pen‑streptomycin (Corning). Incubate at 37 °C for 2 h, wash with PBS, add maintenance DMEM, and keep at 37 °C for 7 days, checking daily for cytopathic effect (CPE). Consider a specimen negative after three blind passages without CPE. Confirm isolates by characteristic CPE (cell rounding, syncytia) and N‑gene RT‑PCR.

substeps.instruction: Prepare inoculum from processed samples and filter (0.2 µm).
Decant old medium from Vero cell flasks and add 1 mL filtered inoculum.
Incubate 2 h at 37 °C.
Wash cells with PBS and replace with fresh DMEM (maintenance).
Maintain cultures at 37 °C for up to 7 days, observing daily for CPE.
If no CPE after three blind passages, record as negative.
Verify positive isolates by N‑gene RT‑PCR.

steps.title: Harvest virus supernatant
steps.instruction: Subject infected Vero cell cultures to three freeze‑thaw cycles, centrifuge the lysate, and collect the clarified supernatant for downstream RNA extraction or antigen preparation.

substeps.instruction: Freeze cells at –80 °C, thaw at room temperature; repeat three times.
Centrifuge the lysate at appropriate speed (as per lab standard).
Collect the supernatant and store at –70 °C until needed.

steps.title: Purify PCR amplicons for sequencing
steps.instruction: Purify the N‑gene PCR products using the QIAEXII PCR Purification Kit (Qiagen) according to the manufacturer’s protocol and ship the purified DNA to Macrogen (Korea) for sequencing.

steps.title: Prepare IELISA antigen
steps.instruction: Precipitate the virus‑containing supernatant with 8 % (w/v) PEG 6000 in 2.3 % (w/v) NaCl, incubate overnight at 4 °C, centrifuge at 8 500 g for 30 min, and dissolve the pellet in TNE buffer (Tris, NaCl, EDTA, pH 7.4) at one‑tenth of the original supernatant volume; store the antigen at –80 °C.

substeps.instruction: Add PEG 6000 to a final concentration of 8 % (w/v) and NaCl to 2.3 % (w/v) to the clarified supernatant.
Mix gently and incubate overnight at 4 °C.
Centrifuge the mixture at 8 500 g for 30 min.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in TNE buffer at a volume equal to one‑tenth of the original supernatant.
Aliquot and store the antigen at –80 °C.

steps.title: Quantify antigen and determine TCID₅₀
steps.instruction: Measure antigen concentration with a BioSpec‑Nano spectrophotometer (Shimadzu) (recorded 455.12 ng/µL, OD 1.92) and determine infectivity as 10⁴·⁸ TCID₅₀/mL using standard TCID₅₀ assay.

steps.title: Optimize IELISA by checkerboard titration
steps.instruction: Perform checkerboard titration of antigen and serum to find the dilution pair giving the greatest positive‑to‑negative absorbance difference at 450 nm. Use reference negative serum (VNT titer 1:4) in two‑fold dilutions starting at 1:2, test true/false positive/negative controls, and adopt a 50 % positivity cutoff for IELISA (cELISA cutoffs 50 % and 60 %).

substeps.instruction: Prepare two‑fold serial dilutions of the reference negative serum beginning at 1:2.
Prepare two‑fold serial dilutions of the antigen.
Plate each antigen‑serum combination in duplicate wells and incubate according to IELISA protocol.
Read absorbance at 450 nm and calculate P/N ratios.
Select the antigen and serum dilutions that yield the maximal P/N difference.
Apply the 50 % positivity cutoff for subsequent testing.

steps.title: Determine optimal serum and antigen dilutions
steps.instruction: From the titration data, choose a serum dilution of 1:200 and an antigen dilution of 1:32 as the optimal working concentrations; confirm that OD values decline beyond these dilutions.

steps.title: Validate assay reproducibility
steps.instruction: Run duplicate serum samples (positive and negative standards) on three independent plates; verify that absorbance values show no significant variation.

steps.title: Test field sera and compare assays
steps.instruction: Analyze 325 field serum samples in parallel with the commercial cELISA kit using the optimized IELISA conditions; record absorbance values and calculate diagnostic performance.

steps.title: Analyze diagnostic performance
steps.instruction: Calculate sensitivity as a/(a + c) × 100 and specificity as d/(d + b) × 100 using true‑positive (a), false‑positive (b), false‑negative (c), and true‑negative (d) counts; perform statistical analysis with GraphPad Prism 5.01.
